primitives.name: Golden Path Role Mapping
primitives.verbatim_quote: Direction confirmed with owner: *map golden-path roles to existing routes, create no new routes, flag genuine gaps.* Golden path (intended): Homepage → Today's Board → Decision Room → Evidence/Trust → Coach → No-Bet/Parlay MRI → Autopsy → Command Center → Academy → Report → Demo.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_i': 'role index in golden path sequence', 'S_i': 'status of role i ∈ {done, stub, mapped, gap}', 'T_i': 'transition time from role i to i+1'}
primitives.assumptions: Each role maps to an existing route; no new routes are created.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When S_i = gap, R_i cannot be traversed without owner intervention.

layer2.mapping: Each role in golden path corresponds to a node in the GSI Bayesian network where S_i determines conditional probability P(R_{i+1}|R_i).
layer2.telemetry: Status badge indicators on UI render S_i values.

primitives.name: Degraded State Rendering
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Degraded-state proof (verified) - Picks/board/performance/observatory/vault all render explicit bootstrap/stub states with status badges + explanatory copy + a link onward when their gate is closed.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'B_i': 'bootstrap state indicator for component i', 'S_i': 'stub state indicator for component i', 'L_i': 'link onward availability for component i'}
primitives.assumptions: All components must display explicit stub or bootstrapped state.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When B_i = false or S_i = true, L_i is disabled until gate opens.

layer2.mapping: Component state vector (B_i, S_i, L_i) drives GSE transition function to determine next valid state.
layer2.telemetry: UI status badges and explanatory copy serve as empirical observables.

primitives.name: Trust Context Linkage
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Trust context reachable from every page via global `Footer`.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C_t': 'trust context node at time t', 'F_p': 'footer element on page p', 'P_p': 'page identifier'}
primitives.assumptions: Global footer ensures universal access to trust context.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If F_p is absent, C_t becomes unreachable for P_p.

layer2.mapping: Each page P_p has a fixed-point trust linkage C_t = f(F_p), ensuring consistent GSI inference across all views.
layer2.telemetry: Footer presence and C_t accessibility verified via DOM inspection.

The golden path defines a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of navigational roles, each mapped to a functional route. The DAG's edges encode transition probabilities based on role statuses (done/stub/gap). In GSI, this translates into a Bayesian belief network where each role contributes a conditional probability P(R_{i+1}|R_i). When a role is flagged as a gap (e.g., Coach), its conditional probability becomes undefined or zero, enforcing a process-over-outcome constraint. Degraded-state rendering introduces stub nodes that act as terminal states in GSE’s finite-state machine, triggering fallback logic when gates are closed. Trust context linkage ensures that all pages maintain a consistent belief state through a global footer, enabling cross-layer coherence in both GSI and GSE. Failure modes occur when mappings are broken (e.g., missing route), stubs are not rendered, or trust context is inaccessible.
